4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Graded this week: your Block Breaker published with a working link turned in on Google Classroom, one new software pattern added (the Component pattern), and a short explanation of which component you picked, why, and how it improves your game.
4th Period.workingNow: Open the Google Classroom assignment called Component Pattern. Read the instructions, follow them, and turn in your game link and your short explanation when you are done.
4th Period.smartGoal: By the end of class, I can plan one component, add it to my Block Breaker with Copilot, publish my game, and explain why I picked it.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.13 — Decompose problems and subproblems into parts to facilitate the design, implementation, and review of programs.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.10 — Writing literary and informational texts to present, describe, and explain ideas and information, using appropriate technology.
agenda: Mini-lesson: the Component pattern and 3 example components (7 min)
Plan first: pick one and plan it with Copilot (8 min)
You do: build your component and test your game (15 min)
Commit, Sync Changes, hard refresh, and check your live game (7 min)
Explain your pick and turn in your link on Google Classroom (8 min)
4th Period.connections: Wednesday you learned that trigger and change is the Event Handler pattern. Today you plan and add a second pattern, Component, by plugging a small piece into your game. Class meets next on Tuesday.

6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Due Sunday night: your Lift the Load document with your arm lengths, a screenshot of the load rising, and your short description.
6th Period.workingNow: Open the Google Classroom assignment called Lift the Load. Read the instructions, follow them, and turn in your work when you are done. There is no exit ticket today.
6th Period.smartGoal: By the end of class, I can set up a lever in the simulator that lifts a 500 N load using only a 150 N effort, and show it with a screenshot.
6th Period.contentStandard: NGSS MS-ETS1-1 — Define the criteria and constraints of a design problem with sufficient precision to ensure a successful solution.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.12 — Selecting and applying varied and precise vocabulary and other language resources to effectively convey ideas.
agenda: Computer rules and read the problem (5 min)
Mini-lesson: the lever rule and an example (5 min)
Solve it in the simulator (22 min)
Screenshot and fill in your document (8 min)
Turn in on Google Classroom (5 min)
6th Period.connections: Wednesday you explored levers by balancing a seesaw. Today you use the lever rule with real numbers to lift a 500 N load. Class meets next on Tuesday.

7th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Due Sunday night: your Build a Pulley document with a photo of your pulley (however far you got) and two sentences about what you did to help.
7th Period.workingNow: Open the Google Classroom assignment called Build a Pulley. Read the instructions, follow them, and turn in your work when you are done. There is no exit ticket today.
7th Period.smartGoal: By the end of class, my group can build a cardboard pulley on a pencil axle and try to lift a water bottle, and I can say what I did to help.
7th Period.contentStandard: NGSS MS-ETS1-4 — Develop a model to generate data for iterative testing and modification of a proposed object, tool, or process.
7th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.12 — Selecting and applying varied and precise vocabulary and other language resources to effectively convey ideas.
agenda: Table jobs, safety rules, and demo (7 min)
Build your pulley wheel and axle (24 min)
Try to lift the water bottle and fix one thing (7 min)
Clean up, take your photo, and write 2 sentences (7 min)
7th Period.connections: Wednesday you explored simple machines on the computer, including the pulley. Today your table builds one from cardboard, a pencil, and string. Class meets next on Tuesday.
